solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: One endless complaint about lacklustre inspiration

indicators.note: about means going around, so the complaint wraps itself round the next word
without an end means the final letter of the word for complaint is dropped

parts.note: one is the article a
a fuss is a complaint or protest
flat means dull, without sparkle

explanation.surface: Someone moans endlessly about a dull, uninspired performance.
explanation.walkthrough: About tells the shortened complaint to wrap round the second word, with the one in front. Afflatus is a rare Latin word, from a breathing upon.
explanation.definitionFit: Afflatus is a literary word for a divine creative impulse, a synonym for inspiration.

clue.text: Ten working in awful serfage? These aren't!

definitions.text: Ten working in awful serfage? These aren't!

indicators.note: working suggests letters set in motion and moved about
awful hints at something mangled into a terrible state, so its letters are jumbled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Ten people toiling in miserable serfdom are certainly not their own masters.
explanation.walkthrough: Serfage is serfdom; the whole clue doubles as the definition, since people bound in serfdom are the opposite of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Free agents act independently and are bound to nobody, which serfs working the land plainly are not.

clue.text: Treasury minister in cricket ground with top Government members

indicators.note: in puts the minister inside the ground, so the ground's name surrounds him

parts.note: Lord's is the famous London cricket ground
the Chancellor of the Exchequer runs the British Treasury

explanation.surface: The finance minister turns up at a cricket match alongside senior cabinet colleagues.
explanation.walkthrough: LORD(CHANCELLOR)S. Lord's in north London is the home of English cricket.
explanation.definitionFit: The Lord Chancellor is a senior cabinet post in British government, so holders of it are top ministers.

clue.text: Ousted Head quietly went first

parts.note: the top is the head of something
p, piano, is the musical direction for quietly
someone who went first led

explanation.surface: A headteacher was forced out after quietly being the first to leave.
explanation.definitionFit: To topple a leader is to overthrow them, so a toppled ruler has been ousted.

clue.text: Rested for a day

definitions.meaning: first meaning: past tense of sit, took a seat
second meaning: the usual abbreviation for Saturday

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests a single day's rest; in fact it holds two separate meanings of one short word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sat is both the past tense of sit, meaning took a rest, and the standard shortening of Saturday.

clue.text: Cut out organ part and remove piano from consideration

indicators.note: remove asks for a letter to be taken away from the following word

parts.note: respect means regard or consideration
p is the musical abbreviation for piano

explanation.surface: A surgeon removes part of an organ and drops the piano from the plans.
explanation.walkthrough: RESPECT without its P gives RESECT.
explanation.definitionFit: To resect is a surgical term meaning to excise part of an organ or tissue.

clue.text: Norway replaces Italy, messing up administration

indicators.note: replaces tells us one letter takes the place of another within a word

parts.note: messing up something is ruining it
N is the international vehicle code for Norway
I is the international vehicle code for Italy

explanation.surface: A Scandinavian team ousts the Italians and botches the management of something.
explanation.walkthrough: In RUINING the first I becomes N, giving RUNNING.
explanation.definitionFit: The running of a business is its management or administration, a noun sense of the word.

clue.text: Married musicians with limitations

parts.note: the strings are the string players of an orchestra
attached means in a committed relationship, spoken for

explanation.surface: Orchestral players who are married find their freedom curtailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The pieces come in reverse clue order: the musicians first, then the word for married.
explanation.definitionFit: Strings attached are conditions or restrictions tied to an offer, so the phrase means limitations.

clue.text: School managed without parking

indicators.note: without asks for the following item to be dropped from the word

parts.note: to cope is to manage
P is the road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A school got by despite having no car park.
explanation.walkthrough: COPED loses its P.
explanation.definitionFit: A co-ed is a coeducational school, one teaching boys and girls together.

clue.text: What we all pass by beginning to rile aristocrat

parts.note: everyone passes water, pee

indicators.note: beginning to points at the opening letter only of the next word

parts.note: first letter of rile

explanation.surface: Something every passer-by does starts to irritate a nobleman.
explanation.walkthrough: The cheeky toilet humour hides behind innocent walking: we all pass water. By means placed next to.
explanation.definitionFit: A peer is a member of the nobility, such as a duke or earl, hence an aristocrat.

clue.text: Russian leader's edict is classified

parts.note: Vladimir Putin, the Russian president
an edict is an official order

explanation.surface: A decree from the Kremlin has been made secret.
explanation.walkthrough: Classified tempts as secret, but here it means sorted.
explanation.definitionFit: Things classified have been sorted into categories, which is arranged or put in order.

clue.text: Call in at once to order shelving

indicators.note: to order means arranging into a new sequence, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: the fodder, taken letter for letter

explanation.surface: An urgent instruction to summon someone to arrange some shelves.
explanation.walkthrough: Shelving looks like storage furniture, but it is the act of shelving a plan.
explanation.definitionFit: Shelving a project means dropping or postponing it, which is a cancellation.

clue.text: Person who's bashed our ears?

indicators.note: something bashed is knocked out of shape, so the letters are battered into a new order

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: Someone has been making a din that assaults our hearing.
explanation.walkthrough: As a whole the clue describes one who rouses people by making noise in their ears.
explanation.definitionFit: An arouser is one who wakes or stirs people up, as a loud noise in the ears does.

clue.text: Don't sustain grassland and ban bull

parts.note: a lea is a meadow
to veto is to forbid
bull is slang for nonsense, as is rot

explanation.surface: A farmer neglects the pasture and forbids a bull.
explanation.walkthrough: Bull looks like livestock beside grassland, but it is short for nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: To leave something to rot is to neglect it and fail to maintain it.

clue.text: Polish annoyed when one of two Poles arrested? Partly

indicators.note: something arrested is held inside, so one item is captured within the other
to polish something is to rework it, so the next word's letters are reworked

parts.note: the fodder letters
S is South, one of the two poles, North and South

explanation.surface: A Pole gets cross when a fellow countryman is taken into custody.
explanation.walkthrough: Polish masquerades as the nationality, and Poles as people; Polish is the anagram signal and Poles are the Earth's poles.
explanation.definitionFit: Answering yes and no means a statement is true only in part, so the phrase means partly.

clue.text: Well and good, I'll indicate your seat at the match

parts.note: G is the abbreviation for good

parts.words: I'll indicate your seat at the match
parts.note: an usher shows guests to their seats, at a wedding match for instance

explanation.surface: A cheerful steward at a ground offers to show you to your seat.
explanation.walkthrough: Match is a marriage here: ushers seat guests at weddings. Well and good looks like a phrase but splits into the definition and G.
explanation.definitionFit: A gusher is an oil well that spouts freely without pumping.

clue.text: Tons in bags?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: tons of something is a great amount
second meaning: bags of something is also plenty

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests weighing sacks of goods, but both words are informal terms for a large quantity.
explanation.definitionFit: Stacks, like tons and bags, is colloquial for lots or a large amount of something.

clue.text: Parts of a larger group fixed loans externally

indicators.note: externally means on the outside, so one word sits around the other

parts.note: subs are advances on wages, small loans
set means fixed or settled

explanation.surface: Fixed-rate borrowing is split into sections of a bigger portfolio.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB(SET)S. A sub is British slang for an advance of money, usually against wages.
explanation.definitionFit: A subset is a group contained within a larger set, in mathematics and generally.

clue.text: Calming influence finally found in second case

indicators.note: found in means sitting inside, so one letter is placed within the rest

parts.note: s is the abbreviation for second

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of influence
the dative is a grammatical case

explanation.surface: A soothing effect was eventually discovered in the second instance.
explanation.walkthrough: Calming influence reads as one phrase and a natural definition, but only Calming defines; influence supplies its last letter, E, which sits in S + DATIVE.
explanation.definitionFit: Sedative as an adjective describes something that soothes or calms the nerves.

clue.text: Blood pressure drug, mostly slow to act

indicators.note: mostly means not quite all, so the final letter is lost

parts.note: dilatory means tardy, slow to act

explanation.surface: A hypertension medicine mostly takes its time to work.
explanation.walkthrough: DILATORY loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A dilator, or vasodilator, widens blood vessels and so is used to lower blood pressure.

clue.text: Political grouping dismayed a pal terribly

indicators.note: dismayed suggests being thrown into disorder, so the letters are put in disarray

parts.note: the fodder letters

explanation.surface: A political faction has upset a friend badly.
explanation.walkthrough: Terribly looks like the anagram signal, but it is fodder; dismayed is the signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The Liberal Party is a political party, a grouping of people sharing political aims.

clue.text: Assistant's suggested course of action: the last shall be first

indicators.note: the biblical saying tells us the final letter moves round to the front

parts.note: an idea is a proposed plan

explanation.surface: A helper offers a plan, quoting scripture about the last becoming first.
explanation.walkthrough: IDEA with its final A moved to the start gives AIDE.
explanation.definitionFit: An aide is a helper or assistant, especially to an official.

clue.text: Old Queen and English authoress made a little contribution

parts.note: Dido was the legendary queen of Carthage
E. Nesbit wrote The Railway Children

explanation.surface: A former queen and an English woman writer each helped out a little.
explanation.walkthrough: Old Queen suggests a British monarch, but it is Dido of Carthage, of Virgil's Aeneid.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing one's bit means playing one's part, making a modest contribution to a shared effort.

clue.text: Roll in bed alongside partner, at first

indicators.note: at first points at the opening letter of each of the words before it

parts.note: initial letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A couple tumble about in bed together, at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Roll looks like a tumble in bed; it is bread. A bap is a soft British bread roll.
explanation.definitionFit: A bap is a large soft bread roll, common in Britain.

clue.text: Daughter separated from cruel guy gets a good guy

indicators.note: separated from means being parted from, so one letter is taken out

parts.note: King Herod ordered the massacre of the innocents
d is the abbreviation for daughter

explanation.surface: A daughter leaves a brutal man and finds a decent one.
explanation.walkthrough: HEROD without D.
explanation.definitionFit: A hero is an admirable figure, the good guy of a story as opposed to the villain.

clue.text: Goes hungry retaining little energy? These should help!

definitions.note: cryptic: these are large helpings, which would aid the hungry

indicators.note: retaining means keeping hold of, so one word holds the other inside

parts.note: to fast is to go without food
e is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Someone starving with barely any energy; this is what would rescue them.
explanation.walkthrough: FA(E)STS. Help hints at helpings of food: the answer is the cure for the fasting.
explanation.definitionFit: Feasts are lavish meals, exactly what would relieve someone who goes hungry.

clue.text: Green minerals (type finally clear in Chambers)

indicators.note: in places the preceding letters inside the following word

parts.note: chambers are chamber pots

indicators.note: finally points at the last letter of the word just before it

parts.note: last letter of type
to rid is to clear

explanation.surface: A note that the green stones are to be looked up in the Chambers dictionary.
explanation.walkthrough: P(E+RID)OTS. Chambers looks like the dictionary publisher, but means chamber pots.
explanation.definitionFit: Peridot is an olive-green gem variety of the mineral olivine.
